components.note: 木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
手 (hand) — 拿 means to take or hold something in the hand
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 拿's reading ná, from an older, closer pronunciation link
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
马 (horse) shows 驾 relates to driving or controlling an animal or vehicle.
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to jià, differing mainly in tone.
马 (horse) — 驶 originally described a horse running swiftly, extending to 'to drive, to sail.'
史 (shǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 驶.
入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
米 (grain, rice) — 糟 originally named the dregs left over from making rice wine.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound close to zāo, sharing the same rhyme and tone.
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
辶 (to walk/move) — 适 relates to fitting well as one moves along, i.e. being suitable
舌 (shé) gives a sound distantly related to 适's reading shì, having drifted apart over a long time
亻 (a person) — someone receiving something
寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'
土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
臼 pictures a clay mortar or vessel.
殳 (a tool, held in a hand) strikes it, giving 毁 its meaning 'to destroy, to smash.'
一 (a horizontal line) depicts something laid over the fire below.
火 (fire) — covering a flame to smother it gave 灭 its meaning 'to extinguish, to go out.'
讠 (speech) — 诅 (to curse) is done through speech.
且 (qiě) gives a sound only distantly related to zǔ today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.

meanings: expression or emotion showing in one's eyes

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'
贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 财's reading cái
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
攵 (an action/to strike) — 攻 relates directly to attacking or striking
工 (gōng) gives the sound — 攻 is also pronounced gōng, an exact match
灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

meanings: to go to a lot of trouble

components.note: 辛 is traditionally read as a picture of a hot branding iron, once used to mark prisoners — a harsh origin behind its meaning 'bitter, laborious.'
艹 (grass/plant) — 苦 relates to the bitter taste of certain plants and herbs
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to 苦's reading kǔ
水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
口 (mouth) — arguing is done vocally.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound fairly close to chǎo, sharing the rhyme.
木 (wood) — racks and frames like 架 were traditionally built of wood.
加 (jiā) gives a rhyme close to jià, with the tone shifted.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

meanings: Europe (abbr. for 歐羅巴洲|欧罗巴洲[Ou1 luo2 ba1 Zhou1])

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water surrounding the land
州 (a stretch of land) — depicted as islands of land within a river
阝 (hill) — 险 originally referred to steep, dangerous terrain
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 险's reading xiǎn, having drifted apart over time

meanings: (Internet slang) first reply to a forum post

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.
弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
女 (woman) — a component whose original link to the meaning has faded, an example of how radicals don't always map cleanly onto meaning.
干 (gān) gives a sound moderately close to jiān, sharing the final but not the initial.
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'
芒 (the tip of a plant, an awn) — 荒 relates to overgrown, uncultivated land.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to huāng, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — 谬 relates to a false or mistaken statement.
翏 (liù) gives a sound only distantly related to miù today, having drifted apart over time.
丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'
Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect
至 (zhì) gives the sound — 致 is also pronounced zhì, an exact match
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'
口 (mouth) — 嘲 relates to speaking, in this case mocking someone.
朝 (cháo) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘲.
夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.
卩 (a kneeling figure) — a hungry person kneeling down, about to eat.
皀 (a bowl of food) — the meal in front of them, giving 即 its sense of imminent action, 'right away, that is to say.'
辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.
